title: fix(service-automation): an installed package's connector entry never reads the host's files
body:
Fixes #28534
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:安装进来的包(install-local / `os package install`,注册表 `source: 'marketplace'`)所声明的连接器条目,不再拿到以宿主根目录为锚的 `loadPackageFile` / `resolvePackagePath`;两个成员对任何相对引用一律拒绝,报错点名条目、包、引用和修法。宿主自己的条目照旧读自己的文件。
- 为什么改:实测在 `a52191f6` 上,一个安装进 showcase 的包声明 `spec: './src/system/connectors/status-openapi.json'`,连接器以 `ready` 上线,用的是宿主 showcase 自己的 OpenAPI 文档;一个 stdio MCP 条目在宿主根目录下跑起了宿主自己的 `scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs`。安装来的包可以靠猜路径绑定别的包的文件。
- 风险与回滚:安装包里依赖包内文件的 `openapi` 条目、以及安装包里所有 stdio `mcp` 条目(工厂总要 `resolvePackagePath('.')`)现在都不再上线,只在对账日志里报错;内联文档与 http(s) URL 不受影响。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`(`installedDeclaringPackageOf` 判定与调用点三元式),`connector-materialization.test.ts` 的 `#28534` 块,dogfood `install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts`,预期 4 passed,日志里两条 ERROR 分别点名 `pkgref_host_file` 与 `pkgref_host_cwd`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`, at the one call site that builds each entry's `ConnectorProviderContext`:

- `installedDeclaringPackageOf(entry, registry)` answers whether the package that declared the entry was installed: it reads the package registry's row for the entry's `_packageId` stamp and its `source`, which the registering door states and the registry records without inferring it. The install-local door registers `'marketplace'` (at install and at every restart's rehydrate); the host's stack, a multi-package artifact's members and plugin packages register `'code'`. Only `'marketplace'` counts as installed. No stamp, a stamp no row answers (a composed stack's residual owner), or no `objectql` registry all read as the host's, exactly as today.
- For an installed entry, both members are `createInstalledPackageRefRefusal(...)`, which rejects every ref, naming the entry, the package, the ref and a remedy per member: `reads` says rebuild with a current `os build` (which carries an `openapi` spec file into the artifact) or inline the document; `paths` says a provider needing a location inside the package (a stdio MCP server's working directory) cannot serve an installed entry, use a transport that needs none.
- Members, not `undefined`: the contract's `undefined` means "this host has no filesystem", and for `resolvePackagePath` the MCP factory then keeps its old behaviour (the child inherits the host's working directory), the same cross-package reach.
- The refusal reaches the materializer as the factory's own throw, so it takes the existing configuration-fault channel unchanged: fatal at boot, logged at `error` and the entry skipped on reload. No new marker, no `packages/spec` change.

Docs: one row in the failure-modes table of `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`. Changeset: `@objectstack/service-automation` patch.

## Tests

- `connector-materialization.test.ts`, new `#28534` block (6 cases): installed entry naming a file the host has is not materialized on reload and nothing is read; the refusal names entry, package, ref and the `os build` remedy, and never the host's path; `resolvePackagePath('.')` takes the same rule; controls: an installed entry carrying its document inline materializes with neither member reached; the host's entries (a `code` row, a stamp no row answers, no stamp) read and resolve under the host root; one refused installed entry leaves a host entry beside it serving.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts` (4 cases) over the real `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` door into the showcase: an installed `openapi` entry naming `./src/system/connectors/status-openapi.json` and an installed stdio `mcp` entry naming `./scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs` are absent from `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors`, each with an error record naming entry, package and ref; controls: an installed inline-document entry lists `ready` with its own operation, and the showcase's own `showcase_status_openapi` and `showcase_mcp_tools` keep listing `ready`.

## Acceptance notes

- PM mechanism assumption measured and partly disproved: the refusal is a configuration fault for that one entry and the install still answers 200, but on the reload path a configuration fault is logged and the entry is skipped; it is NOT visible on `GET /automation/connectors` or as a held husk (a husk exists only for an instance that was already degraded). That is the existing channel for every configuration fault of an installed entry, kept as is.
- Boot: an install-local package registers at `kernel:ready`, after the fatal boot reconcile in `start()`, so its entries meet only the soft reconcile in this repository's composition. Measured with a throwaway probe at `71597f1b` (not committed): install, stop, boot again on the same ledger; the second boot raised no error. A boot artifact whose `packages[]` entry states `source: 'marketplace'` (no producer in this repository) would meet the fatal one, exactly as a missing file does today.
- Seen by the same probe and outside this card: after the restart the package is rehydrated (listed by `GET /marketplace/install-local`) but neither of its connectors is on `GET /automation/connectors`, including the inline-document one, which never reaches the changed members. Reported for filing, not fixed here.
- Behaviour change to read before landing: every stdio `mcp` entry of an installed package is now refused, whatever its command, because the MCP factory always asks `resolvePackagePath('.')`. An installed package has no directory to run it in; before this it ran in the host's.
- Scope kept to the ruling's "installed": the registry's third source, `'authored'` (packages written through `POST /api/v1/packages` or Studio), keeps today's host-root reading. Whether such a package can carry a provider-bound connector entry was not measured. Raised as an open question in the report, not decided here.
- The `reads` remedy names a current `os build`, which carries the `openapi` spec file into the artifact since PR #28533; that PR is merged into this branch (`2be3fd45`), as is PR #28515, which added a branch beside this call site.
